mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) over the past 6 months signals robust demand growth, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDPC1's quarterly trend reverses downward or 20-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05) over the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 2%, signaling monetary easing, it reduces borrowing costs, stimulating corporate investment and equity demand, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS does not fall below 2% within the next month, or 5-day returns are not positively correlated with the rate change (Pearson r <0.3).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand across sectors, amplifying growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 returns positively over 20 days.
failure_condition: The proxies GDPC1 and HOUST do not move in tandem (Pearson correlation <0.5) over the 20-day horizon, or returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% suggests labor market weakening, triggering inflation concerns and negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE stays below 5% or 5-day returns are not negatively correlated with UNRATE changes (Pearson r >-0.3).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 105 signals supply-side pressures, leading to inflationary risks and negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 105 in the late-cycle regime, or 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) alongside strong GDP growth (GDPC1) creates a conflicting signal: higher rates may pressure valuations, but robust demand offsets this, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 do not move in the expected conflicting pattern (e.g., FEDFUNDS up while GDPC1 also up), or returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 240, signaling accelerating price pressures, it triggers investor concerns about rate hikes, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not exceed 240 within the next month, or 5-day returns are not negatively correlated with CPI changes (Pearson r < -0.3).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery regime, a sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% indicates labor market stabilization, fostering confidence and positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE does not rise above 4% in the post-shock regime, or 60-day returns are not positively correlated with UNRATE changes (Pearson r >0.3).
